what: India rules, rates and practice facts the Ask may state, each with the date it was checked and its source (Madhav, 27 Oct 2026: the outside review found the Ask out of date or silent on tax, broker practice and regulation). Not pinned; refresh after each Budget, RBI policy meeting and SEBI circular.

facts.fact: Listed shares and equity mutual funds: held more than 12 months, gains are long-term and taxed at 12.5% on the part above Rs 1.25 lakh of long-term gains in a financial year; held 12 months or less, gains are short-term and taxed at 20%. Surcharge and cess come on top. Budget 2026 left these unchanged.

The concessional equity rates apply only when STT was paid on the transfer; there is no indexation on listed equity; for shares bought before 1 Feb 2018 the cost can be taken as the 31 Jan 2018 market price (grandfathering, section 112A).

From FY 2025-26 the section 87A rebate (the 'no tax up to Rs 12 lakh' of the new regime) does not cover capital gains taxed at special rates: short-term equity gains (section 111A) and long-term equity gains (112A) are still taxed even when total income is under Rs 12 lakh.

Since 1 Apr 2025: gold ETFs held more than 12 months and gold mutual funds / gold fund-of-funds held more than 24 months are long-term, taxed at 12.5% without indexation; shorter holdings are taxed at the investor's slab rate.

A gold fund (fund-of-funds) such as SBI Gold Fund invests in its fund house's gold ETF, so the investor pays the fund's expense ratio on top of the ETF's; buying the gold ETF directly is cheaper but needs a demat account.
No new Sovereign Gold Bond tranches have been issued since February 2024; existing bonds can be bought and sold on the exchange and redeemed early on RBI's schedule.

Every mutual fund scheme has a Direct plan (bought from the fund house or a direct platform, no distributor commission) and a Regular plan (through a distributor, a higher expense ratio). Same portfolio; the Regular plan's NAV grows slower by the extra cost every year, often 0.5-1.5% a year for equity funds.
facts.source: standard practice: Direct plans exist since SEBI's 2013 rule; the cost gap is visible in each scheme's Direct vs Regular NAV

facts.fact: Most equity funds charge an exit load (commonly 1%) if units are redeemed within 12 months of purchase, and each SIP instalment has its own 12-month clock; switching funds is a redemption, so it can trigger both exit load and capital-gains tax.
facts.source: standard practice: each scheme's document states its exit load

facts.fact: SPIVA India (S&P): over the 10 years to December 2025, 76.3% of Indian large-cap funds and 79.0% of mid/small-cap funds underperformed their benchmark index.
SEBI's study of FY2024-25: 91% of individual traders in equity derivatives (F&O) lost money; their net losses were about Rs 1.06 lakh crore.

From 1 Apr 2026 (Budget 2026), STT on futures rose from 0.02% to 0.05% of the sale value and on options from 0.10% to 0.15% of the premium sold (0.15% on exercise); STT on cash-market shares was unchanged.
Index derivative lot sizes since the January 2026 contracts: Nifty 50 = 65, Bank Nifty = 30, Fin Nifty = 60, Midcap Nifty (Nifty Midcap Select) = 120.

Bracket orders have not been available at Zerodha (and several other brokers) since March 2020; the usual substitutes are a GTT OCO order (a target and a stop that cancel each other, for delivery holdings) and a cover order (entry plus a compulsory stop, intraday).

Before paying anyone for market advice or investing through them, check they are SEBI-registered (SEBI's intermediary search) and pay only to a validated '@valid' UPI handle, which can be checked with the SEBI Check tool; unregistered tip groups promising multi-bagger returns are a common pump-and-dump pattern. Report them on SEBI SCORES.
RBI repo rate: 5.50%, raised by 25 basis points from 5.25% at the 7 Oct 2026 policy meeting, with the stance changed from neutral to 'calibrated tightening'.

Ananta's one rule of thumb: keep 6 months of living expenses as an emergency fund (9-12 months if income is uncertain) in a savings account, FD or liquid fund, separate from investments; get term and health insurance in place before investing for growth.
facts.source: standard Indian personal-finance practice (Ananta's house rule)

facts.fact: Borrowing to invest in shares means paying a fixed interest rate (personal loans often 11-20% a year) for an uncertain return that can be negative for years; no market condition makes a personal loan for stocks sensible.
facts.source: standard practice; RBI repo 5.50% (lending rates sit well above it)

facts.fact: Selling a holding at a loss books a capital loss that can be set off against capital gains (short-term losses against short- or long-term gains; long-term losses only against long-term gains) and carried forward 8 years if the return is filed on time; selling at a gain books a taxable gain.
facts.source: Income-tax Act, sections 70-74 (set-off and carry-forward of capital losses)
